newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian stock exchange begins trading.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian stock exchange begins trading.

text.p: Palestinians launched a stock market Tuesday, with limited trading at an exchange in the West Bank town of Nablus, officials said.
The first two transactions were shown on a screen moments after the exchange was officially opened at 10.01 a.m. local time.
Officials of the exchange broke into applause when a screen flashed the completion of the first transaction -- 100 shares of the Arab Insurance Co. sold for four Jordanian dinars ($5.60) each.
A smaller transaction followed of 10 shares in the Arab Real Estate Co., which were sold for 11 dinars each.
"This is an exciting moment. In fact I can see my wife in the background shedding a drop or two of tears," said Safwan Bataina, Palestine Securities Exchange general manager.

He said the exchange would hold one weekly trading session during an introductory phase, which would last a few weeks. Regular trading, with several sessions per week, would begin as trading volume builds up, he said.
Daily market data is to be published and a market index, to be called the Jerusalem Index, would be added after the introductory phase, Bataina said.
Officials said 23 companies were listed on the exchange for trading and that 20 others were in the process of being listed.
They estimated there were some 60 joint-stock companies in the West Bank and Gaza Strip with estimated combined market capitalisation of $700 million that are eligible for listing.
The $2 million electronic exchange was set up to help attract long-term investment from expatriate Palestinians.

"This exchange is very important because its launching comes at a time when our economy is overcoming problems and entering the phase of development," Palestinian Finance Minister Mohammed Zuhdi al-Nashashibi said moments before the opening.

Nashashibi said Israeli closures of the West Bank and Gaza Strip that impede trade remain a threat to the Palestinian economy and the exchange. He said Palestinian negotiators were pressing the Jewish state to end the closures.

Four brokerage firms based in Nablus and Ramallah are registered to do business at the exchange, and traders and brokers have undergone training. Jordan-based Arab Bank is the clearing house for trading.
Until now, informal trading in some West Bank and Gaza companies was carried through money changers or through the company whose shares were being traded.
